title: The Ten Commandments
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child outlines what the Ten Commandments command (Exodus 20:3-17): worship God alone, no idols, honour God's name, keep the Sabbath holy, honour parents, do not murder, commit adultery, steal, give false witness or covet; without numbering them, as churches number them differently.

floor.question: What does Exodus 20:12 tell children to do?

representations: two tablets drawn: towards God, towards people
steps: Sort commands into God and people.
contexts: keeping Sunday for worship and rest

board.do: Draw two tablets: God and people.
Point at the card "Honour your father and your mother".
board.say: Which tablet does this go on?

board.do: Wait for the child to say people.

listen_for: Give a tenth of your harvest
misconceptions.ask: Which is one of the Ten Commandments?
misconceptions.repair: Read Exodus 20:3-17 and tick each command; the tithe is not there.

misconceptions.ask: Which is not in the Ten Commandments?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list from the passage and check any statement against it.

listen_for: You shall not give false witness
misconceptions.ask: Otieno takes a pen that is not his. Which command does that break?
misconceptions.repair: Match situation cards to command cards, one at a time, reading the command aloud.

misconceptions.ask: To whom did God give the Ten Commandments?
misconceptions.repair: Read Exodus 19:20 and 20:1: God spoke on Mount Sinai and gave the law through Moses.

checks.question: Which of these is one of the Ten Commandments: give a tenth, or honour your parents?
Otieno takes a pen that is not his. Which command does that break?

skills.key_step: The child names the values and life skills in the Ten Commandments (respect, honesty, faithfulness, contentment, self-control, love for God and neighbour) and lessons for today.

floor.question: Which command protects other people's property?

steps: Say what the value looks like there.
contexts: telling the truth in a test
being content without a new phone

board.do: Draw a two-column chart: command and value.
Point at "You shall not give false witness".
Wait for the child to say honesty.
Fill in the rest of the chart.

misconceptions.ask: Which value does "honour your father and your mother" teach?
misconceptions.repair: Write each command with its value: honour parents, respect; do not lie, honesty; do not steal, honesty and contentment.

misconceptions.ask: The Ten Commandments guide how we treat...
misconceptions.repair: Sort the commands on two tablets: God and people. Most are about how we treat others.

misconceptions.ask: Juma wants his classmate's new bag so much that he plans to take it. Which command warns about this?
misconceptions.repair: Explain covet: wanting what is someone else's so much that it rules you. Contrast with admiring and being content.

listen_for: No, they were only for long ago
misconceptions.ask: Do the Ten Commandments teach anything for today?
misconceptions.repair: Read Matthew 22:37-39: Jesus sums up the law as loving God and neighbour. Match each command to today.

checks.question: Which value does "honour your father and mother" teach?
Do the Ten Commandments guide how we treat God only?
